# SequencePlayer

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("SequencePlayer")`

Plays a sequence: a cutscene stored as a file of tracks over time. A sequence can have a camera that cuts and moves, clips on characters, spoken lines, sounds, keyed properties on any instance, morph targets, and events for scripts. Create one anywhere, set `Sequence` to the file, add a `SequenceBinding` child for each name the file expects, and call `Play`.

A sequence runs on simulation time. `TimePosition` advances each tick, so every key and event lands on the same tick in a replay or a headless run. Keyed properties, clips, lines, sounds and events are applied in the tick. The camera and the morph targets are visual only and are computed every frame on each machine.

The sequence controls a keyed property from the first key of its track to the last. Before the first key the sequence does not touch the property. After the last key the property keeps its value and the game can set it again.

While a sequence plays with `TakesCamera` on, the main view is drawn through the camera track. `Workspace.CurrentCamera` is not changed, the game's camera script keeps running, and the view returns to the game's camera when the sequence ends.

In a multiplayer match, a sequence that the authority plays is seen on every machine. Only the fact that it is playing and its start time are replicated; each machine reads the file from its own build. A client that joins late sees the sequence from its current position. A sequence that a client creates plays only on that client.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Controls` | `Enum.SequenceControl` | `Enum.SequenceControl.Keep` | read/write | What happens to player input while the sequence plays. `Suspend` holds the local players' movement and actions at rest on this machine and restores them when the sequence ends. Input events still reach scripts, so a game can bind a key to `Skip`. |
| `Held` | `string` | — | read-only | The name of the hold the sequence is waiting at, or an empty string. A key on a `hold` track stops the sequence's time until `Release` is called, to wait for a choice or a button press. What the sequence already started continues, such as a playing clip, and nothing new starts. |
| `Length` | `number` | — | read-only | The length of the sequence, in seconds. It is available as soon as `Sequence` is set, and is 0 if the file does not exist.<br><br>The length is the end of the last key or the last line, or the length the file states if that is greater. A line lasts as long as its longest language, so the length is the same in every language. |
| `Looped` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the sequence starts again when it reaches the end. A looped sequence does not fire `Finished` on its own; `Skip` still ends it. |
| `Playing` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether the sequence is advancing. Change it with `Play` and `Pause`. |
| `Sequence` | `Content` | — | read/write | The sequence file, as an `asset://` path ending in `.sequence.json`. It is read when first played and again whenever the file changes. |
| `Speed` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How fast the sequence's time runs relative to simulation time. Lines and sounds always play at their own speed. |
| `TakesCamera` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether each machine's main view is drawn through the camera track while the sequence plays. When it is off, the camera track is ignored. |
| `TimePosition` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The current position in the sequence, in seconds. Setting it seeks: every track is put in the state it has at that time, and no event fires. The sequence stays playing or paused as it was. A value beyond `Length` is clamped to `Length`. |

## Methods

### `BindCamera(fn: (cframe: CFrame, fieldOfView: number, time: number) -> (CFrame?, ...number))`

Binds a function that can adjust the camera on every frame in which this sequence has the view. Use it for what a file cannot know, such as a wall the scene happens to be next to.

The function receives the `CFrame` the sequence computed, the field of view in degrees and the sequence's time in seconds. It returns a `CFrame` to draw instead, then optionally a field of view; return nil for either to keep the sequence's value. It runs in a render step, so `GetRenderCFrame` returns drawn positions inside it, and it must not yield.

A player has one such function; binding again replaces it. It applies only on the machine that binds it.

### `GetMarkers(): { { Name: string, Time: number } }`

Returns the sequence's markers, in order of time: the keys of its `marker` track, which usually mark where each shot begins. Returns an empty list if the file has none or does not exist.

### `LoadSequence(sequence: { [string]: any })`

Loads a sequence from a table instead of a file. The table has the same shape as a `.sequence.json` file: `{ format = "sequence", version = 1, bindings = {...}, tracks = {...} }`. `Sequence` is set to a generated name, and `Play` plays the table. Use it for a scene that the game builds as it runs. Raises an error that names the place if the table is not a valid sequence.

The sequence exists only on the machine that loads it. Loaded on a server, it changes the world and every client sees the change, but the visual tracks (camera, fade, bars, morph targets) are not drawn on clients, which do not have the table. For a scene that every machine should see in full, use a file, write the parts that vary as `"$Name"` and set them as attributes.

### `Pause()`

Stops the sequence's time at its current position. The camera stays on the sequence, lines that are being spoken finish, and `Play` resumes it.

### `Play()`

Plays the sequence from its current position: from the start the first time or after it ended, and otherwise from where `Pause` left it.

### `PlayFrom(marker: string): boolean`

Seeks to a marker by name and plays from there. The seek works like setting `TimePosition`: every track is put in the state it has at that time, and no event fires. Returns false and does nothing if the file has no marker of that name.

### `Release()`

Continues from the hold the sequence is waiting at. Does nothing if it is not held. `Play` does the same. In a multiplayer match only the server can call it, like `Play`: a hold is held and released on every machine.

### `Skip()`

Ends the sequence and leaves the world as the sequence would have left it at its end. Every keyed property and morph target takes the value of its last key, and every event between the current position and the end fires in order with `skipped` true. The lines and sounds it started end, clips fade out, characters are set down where their last keys put them, and the camera is returned. Then `Finished` fires with `skipped` true.

### `SkipToNext(): boolean`

Skips to the next marker after the current position and plays on from there. The world is left as the sequence would have left it at that time: keyed properties take the values their keys give them, events in between fire with `skipped` true, and lines and sounds in between are not played. Holds on the way are passed. Returns false and does nothing if there is no later marker; use `Skip` to end the sequence.

### `Stop()`

Ends the sequence and leaves the world as it is at that moment. Properties keep the values the sequence gave them, clips fade out, the lines and sounds it started end, characters it was carrying are set down, the camera is returned, and its time goes back to 0. No event fires, including `Finished`.

### `UnbindCamera()`

Removes the function bound with `BindCamera`. Does nothing if none is bound.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `EventReached(name: string, data: any, skipped: boolean)`

Fires when the sequence reaches a key on an event track. Passes the event's `name` and its `data` as written in the file: a number, a boolean, a string, a list of numbers, or nil.

`skipped` is true for an event fired by `Skip` on the way to the end. A handler that changes the game, such as opening a door, should still act; one that only plays an effect can ignore it. Seeking fires no events.

### `Finished(skipped: boolean)`

Fires when the sequence ends: it reached its end, or `Skip` was called, in which case `skipped` is true. `Stop` does not fire it.

### `HoldReached(name: string)`

Fires when the sequence reaches a key on a `hold` track and starts waiting for `Release`. Passes the hold's name. It fires on every machine.

### `MarkerReached(name: string)`

Fires when the sequence reaches a marker, either by playing through it or by `SkipToNext` landing on it. Passes the marker's name.
